title: Distance to original: the gap catalogue
preamble: This catalogue compares the original Java of four estates with the modern Java that MlCpu.Modernize generated from the J3S COBOL of that Java (original Java → J3S → COBOL → MlCpu.Modernize → modern Java). The original Java is the held-out answer key: the generator never sees it, and nothing here changes a generator. It is measurement and design input for generic generator rules, which another session specifies.

Each estate's measurements are in `compare/<estate>/compare-report.md` (and `.json`): type alignment, API, name and signature fidelity, idioms, structure, the top 20 types by distance, and every gap instance. `jobol-audit compare-gaps` groups the instances into the patterns below. The patterns, their classes and their hypotheses come from `compare-catalogue.json`; the counts and examples come from the reports. Regenerate with `tools/jobol-auditor/compare-estates.sh` and do not edit this file by hand.
Read the counts with three facts in mind.

1. **J3S compiles only what the estate's jobs reach.** Most of the original API that is missing from modern Java was never compiled to COBOL, so no generator could restore it. The `--cobol` option reads the J3S CLASS headers and FRAME comments. Methods with no frame are reported as `METHOD.UNREACHED_*` (pattern G27), not as losses. "Reached" API preservation is the generator's own score: 93.3% for joda-money, 79.4% for kontor-zins, 90.9% for loanamorti and 83.7% for fineract-xl. Every method J3S reached is present in modern Java: `METHOD.MISSING_*` and `OVERLOAD.COLLAPSED` are zero in all four estates (G29). The overloads that looked collapsed were overloads J3S never compiled.

2. **Idioms are compared over the comparable part.** On the original side, idiom and type-use counts leave out methods with no modern counterpart. The reports show both columns ("original, all" and "original").

3. **Pipeline infrastructure is not a gap.** The generated job, platform, record and strangler layers have no original. They are classified by the auditor's lanes (`default-jobol.json`: `**/batch/platform/**`, `**/record/**`, `**/strangler/**` and others are compat) and by `compareInfrastructureGlobs` (`**/batch/**`, the application layer). That covers 36, 37, 37 and 50 modern-only types. They are counted, and are not listed as gaps.

Hypotheses name the COBOL-side evidence a rule could use. The evidence types are these. FRAME comments (`* FRAME OF M0515-LSPAR-NEW LoanScheduleParams.<init>(int, int, ..., Money>, ...)`) give full method names and parameter types by their last dotted segment, so a generic parameter keeps only its last type argument (`Money>`). ENTRY and SRC comments give externally called functions and the original source line spans. CLASS headers give the compiled classes. Data names are cut (frame locals and parameters keep 12 characters, `F0516-L-LOAN-TERM-IN`). There are PICTURE sizes, EVALUATE shapes, the exception class-id tables (`JO-SIMPLE-NAME`), and the identifiers the generated estate already spells out.

patterns.title: Truncated identifiers the estate can complete
patterns.description: A field, parameter, local, method or constant whose modern spelling is the original with its tail cut (`totalFeeChargesChar` for `totalFeeChargesCharged`, `termInMont`). Exactly one identifier elsewhere in the modern estate extends the cut name and it is the original (unique-correct), or several do and the original is one of them (ambiguous-correct). Cut lengths cluster at 10–11 characters (frame locals and parameters) and spread over 14–24 for fields (the 30-character COBOL name, less the prefix).
patterns.evidence: The full spelling survives elsewhere in the COBOL-derived estate: FRAME comments give full method names (`addTotalFeeChargesCharged`), getter and setter names give property names, and assignment `this.loanTermInDays = loanTermIn` links a cut parameter to a full field.
patterns.hypothesis: Complete a cut name to the identifier it flows to or from: a parameter stored into a field takes the field's name, a field returned by a getter takes the property name, and an argument passed to a parameter takes the parameter's name. Only when no data-flow link exists, take the unique estate identifier the cut name is a prefix of. With several candidates, decide only by data flow, never by prefix length.

patterns.title: Truncated identifiers with no or a misleading completion
patterns.description: Cut names that no estate identifier completes (`amountToAd` for `amountToAdd`, `actualPayme`, `disbursementDueDat`, `EARLY_PAYMENT_AMOUNT_IS` for `..._NEGATIVE`), or that a prefix match would complete to the wrong word (unique-wrong, ambiguous-wrong). This is the largest name gap. A counter appended to a cut stem (`scheduleModel2` for `scheduleModelCopy`, `paidAmounts2`) marks two cut names that collided.
patterns.evidence: None in the COBOL: the cut data name (12 characters for a local or parameter, the 30-character name for a field) is all that J3S keeps, and the estate does not spell the word out anywhere.
patterns.hypothesis: Prefix completion with a lexicon (English and banking words): external knowledge, for example a dictionary or a language model limited to completions of the cut stem that are type-compatible. Never apply estate-prefix completion when it is unique-wrong: in fineract-xl it would be wrong 98+21 times. When unsure, keep the cut name. Completing both names of a collision removes the counter.

patterns.title: COBOL abbreviations left unexpanded
patterns.description: Word-by-word abbreviations: enum constants `CAP_INC` (CAPITALIZED_INCOME), `INT_RATE_CHANGE`, `PRIN_GRACE_LIFTED`, `DISB_DATE`, and fields `downPaymentPct` and `disbursedAmountPctF` (`disbursedAmountPercentageForDownPayment`). Most are words the generator's own abbreviation table (MODERNIZATION.md: CAP, INC, INT, PRIN, DISB...) already expands for fields and variables.
patterns.evidence: The learned abbreviation table (paragraph names beside method names). For PCT, the full spelling is in a reached getter's FRAME (`getDisbursedAmountPercentageForDownPayment`).
patterns.hypothesis: Apply the learned abbreviation table to enum constants and static constant names too. Learn new pairs such as PCT and PERCENTAGE from FRAME method names that contain both forms.

patterns.title: Accessors invented in the wrong style
patterns.description: Where J3S never compiled an accessor, the generator invents one in the bean style even when the estate uses record-style accessors. kontor-zins `Schedule.installments()` becomes `getInstallments()`. Invented getters also carry cut field names (`getDisbursedAmountPctF`) or a doubled prefix (`isIsInterestRecalculationE`).
patterns.evidence: The reached accessors' FRAME names give the estate's convention (`LoanTerms.principal()`, `Installment.month()`), and the field's full name (G01).
patterns.hypothesis: Name invented accessors in the convention of the reached accessors of the same type, falling back to the estate's convention. Build the name from the completed field name. Never prefix `is` to a name that already starts with `is`.

patterns.title: Counter names where the original has none
patterns.description: A counter appended to an otherwise exact name (`countryCode3`, `daysInYear3`). These are rare.
patterns.evidence: The base name is exact, so the counter comes from the generator's scope de-duplication, not from the COBOL.
patterns.hypothesis: Add a counter only when the name actually clashes in the same Java scope. Otherwise keep the base name.

patterns.title: Other renames and word-case changes
patterns.description: Word case or separator changes (`calculatedEMI` to `calculatedEmi`, `intToEnumMap` to `INT_TO_ENUM_MAP`) and a few renames (`rp`, `list`, `repaymentEvery` for `repayEvery`, where the abbreviation table over-expanded). Some renames pair two locals by type and are alignment noise.
patterns.evidence: Case does not survive COBOL's upper-case names.
patterns.hypothesis: Low value. At most, do not expand an abbreviation the estate itself uses in reached FRAME names (`repayEvery`).

patterns.title: Generic type arguments erased to Object
patterns.description: `Map<LocalDate,Money>` becomes `Map<Object,Object>`, `Set<Integer>` becomes `Set<Object>`, and `Supplier<? extends T>` becomes `Supplier<Object>`, in fields, parameters and returns. Generic arguments are dropped or changed (`List<T>` to `List<?>`). The modern code then casts at every use.
patterns.evidence: FRAME parameter lists keep the last type argument as a dangling `>` (`Money>` for `Map<LocalDate,Money>`). The modern code's own casts at get, put and iteration sites (`(LocalDate) k`) give the others.
patterns.hypothesis: Type a collection by its frame `X>` token for the last argument and by the unique cast type at its use sites for the others. Remove the casts that become redundant.

patterns.title: Generic type parameters lost
patterns.description: Generic classes and methods become monomorphic: `Memo<T>` and `<T> generateInterestScheduleModel(List<T>, Function<T,LocalDate>, ...)` lose their type parameter.
patterns.evidence: COBOL is monomorphic. Only the different cast types at each instantiation hint at a parameter.
patterns.hypothesis: Introduce a type variable where one Object-typed slot is cast to different types at different call sites. This needs type inference beyond the COBOL evidence, so the type parameter's existence is an external judgement. Low frequency.

patterns.title: Types outside the J3S closure become Object
patterns.description: Fields and parameters whose type J3S never compiled are declared `Object` (`LoanCharge`, `LoanRepaymentScheduleTransactionProcessor`, `LoanCapitalizedIncomeType`). The name is lost even though the COBOL carries it.
patterns.evidence: FRAME parameter lists name the simple type (`LoanScheduleParams.<init>(..., LoanRepaymentScheduleTransactionProcessor, ...)`).
patterns.hypothesis: Declare an opaque boundary type with the frame's simple name (an empty interface in a boundary package, documented as outside the estate) instead of `Object`, or at least keep the name in the declaration.

patterns.title: Known types become Object
patterns.description: Types the estate or the JDK declares are still typed `Object`, mostly fields that reached code only stores and never reads: `DisbursementData.note` and `linkAccountId` (String), `DateUtils.DEFAULT_DATE_FORMATTER` (DateTimeFormatter) and `BigMoney.PARSE_REGEX` (Pattern). Return types are affected too (`Money.zero(MonetaryCurrency)` returns `Object`).
patterns.evidence: The constructor and setter FRAMEs that write the field carry the parameter type (`String`, `Money`). Static initialisers call a typed factory (`Pattern.compile`).
patterns.hypothesis: Type a field by the frame types of the parameters assigned to it, or by the result type of its initialiser call. Type a method's return by the declared type of what it returns.

patterns.title: Interface types replaced by an implementation
patterns.description: Parameters, fields and returns declared with an implementation instead of the original interface or supertype: `ILoanConfigurationDetails` becomes `LoanConfigurationDetails`, and the `LoanAmortizationCalculator` returned by the factories becomes `LoanAmortizationCalculatorImpl` or `AnnualPaymentLoanCalculator`.
patterns.evidence: FRAME parameter lists print the declared type (`shouldRecalculateTillInstallmentDueDate(ILoanConfigurationDetails, boolean)`). The generator already recovers `ILoanConfigurationDetails` from dispatch.
patterns.hypothesis: Declare a parameter with its frame type whenever the estate declares that type, even when one implementation flows in. Do the same for fields assigned from such parameters.

patterns.title: Primitive width, boxing and varargs drift
patterns.description: `short` becomes `int` (joda `CurrencyUnit.numericCode` and `decimalPlaces`), `Integer` becomes `int` (`periodNumber()`), and `Object...` becomes `Object[]` (MathUtil, AbstractPlatformException).
patterns.evidence: PIC S9(4) COMP against S9(9)/S9(10) COMP gives short against int. The `-C` null-flag item beside a numeric item gives a boxed type. Frames print varargs as arrays (`BigDecimal[]`), so restoring varargs needs the JDK convention (class b for that subcase).
patterns.hypothesis: Map PICTURE sizes to the narrowest Java primitive J3S could have produced, and keep the boxed type where the item has a null flag. Make a trailing array parameter varargs when every call site builds a fresh array.

patterns.title: Collection interface drift
patterns.description: The declared collection interface changes: `ConcurrentMap` becomes `Map`, `Collection` becomes `List`, and `Temporal` becomes `LocalDate`.
patterns.evidence: Frames print only the last type argument, not the outer collection type. The JDK emulation program (`JConcurrentHashMap`, `JArrayList`) names the implementation, not the declared interface.
patterns.hypothesis: Choose the narrowest JDK interface that the operations used on the value need (JDK knowledge): `ConcurrentMap` when `putIfAbsent` or `computeIfAbsent` is used, and `Collection` when only iteration and `size` are.

patterns.title: JDK interfaces lost
patterns.description: `Comparable<BigMoneyProvider>`, `Comparable<CurrencyUnit>` and `Serializable` are dropped, along with the `serialVersionUID` constants (joda-money, loanamorti DTOs).
patterns.evidence: `compareTo(X)` FRAMEs exist (`BigMoney.compareTo(BigMoneyProvider)`). Serializable and serialVersionUID leave no trace in the COBOL.
patterns.hypothesis: Implement `Comparable<X>` when a public `int compareTo(X)` exists (a JDK convention). Serializable cannot be recovered from the evidence; at most, use a policy for DTO-like types.

patterns.title: Domain interfaces and superclasses lost: concrete classes only
patterns.description: Domain interfaces disappear from `implements` (`LoanAmortizationCalculator`, `RepeatableEarlyPayment`, `BigMoneyProvider` on Money, `LoanScheduleGenerator`, `ApiFacingEnum`, `LoanPrincipalRelatedDataHolder`). Exception superclasses fall back to `RuntimeException` (`CurrencyMismatchException extends IllegalArgumentException`), and an abstract class becomes concrete (`CurrencyUnitDataProvider`).
patterns.evidence: Interface simple names appear in FRAME parameter types (`BigMoney.of(BigMoneyProvider)`), and the classes whose instances flow there implement them. The generator already recovers `ILoanConfigurationDetails` from dispatch. Exception class ids and catch-site tests give subtyping. A class with no `NEW` site and with subclasses is abstract.
patterns.hypothesis: When an estate type is named in frame parameter or return types and has no CLASS program of its own, declare it an interface whose methods are the ones called on it. Make the classes whose instances reach it implement it. Take an exception's superclass from the catch sites that include its class id. Keep a class abstract when it is never instantiated and has subclasses.

patterns.title: Streams, lambdas and method references lowered to loops
patterns.description: Over the comparable code of fineract-xl, `stream()` calls fall from 79 to 0, method references from 56 to 0 and lambdas from 153 to 88, while loops rise from 40 to 111 (ProgressiveEMICalculator alone: −120 stream, lambda and reference uses, +47 loops). loanamorti shows the same in LoanAmortizationCalculatorImpl.
patterns.evidence: J3S lambda frames (`FRAME OF M0998-LSP-LAMBDA lambda LSP:50`) with their SRC line spans, and the iterator loops over the JDK emulation programs (`JArrayListItr`).
patterns.hypothesis: Raise canonical loop shapes back to the Stream API using JDK knowledge: accumulate into a new list (map, filter, toList), exit early on a boolean (anyMatch, allMatch), sum or reduce, and a min or max scan (min with a Comparator). A lambda frame whose body is a single call becomes a method reference. Do it only when the loop has no other side effects.

patterns.title: Switch expressions and pattern matching not restored
patterns.description: Over the comparable code of fineract-xl, switch expressions fall from 10 to 0 (ProgressiveEMICalculator 6, DaysInMonthType, DaysInYearType, InterestPeriod, ProgressiveLoanInterestScheduleModel). `instanceof` pattern variables are also lost (joda BigMoney and Money, fineract LoanSchedulePlan and Memo).
patterns.evidence: The EVALUATE shape: every WHEN assigns the same target or returns. A type test followed by a cast of the same reference.
patterns.hypothesis: This is a Java-level rewrite that needs no original. Turn a switch or if chain whose branches all assign one variable, or all return, into a switch expression. Turn `instanceof T` followed by `(T) x` into a pattern variable.

patterns.title: Optional returned as nullable or sentinel
patterns.description: The data does not support this as a recurring gap. There is one instance in fineract-xl, and over the comparable code the modern side uses Optional more than the original did (39 against 80 in fineract-xl). Original Optional-returning methods were mostly never compiled by J3S.
patterns.evidence: The JOptional emulation program shows where Optional was used.
patterns.hypothesis: No rule needed now. Re-measure when more Optional-heavy code is reached.

patterns.title: Records lowered to classes
patterns.description: Original records become classes with the same members: kontor-zins `LoanTerms` and `Installment`. Both have a compact constructor that validates and normalises (`principal = Rounding.money(principal)`), and `LoanTerms` has a static constant.
patterns.evidence: All instance fields are final and assigned once from the constructor parameters in declaration order, and the accessors are named exactly as the fields. The generator already turns such classes into records elsewhere (G20).
patterns.hypothesis: Extend record recovery to constructors with a validation or normalisation prologue (emit a compact constructor) and to classes with static members.

patterns.title: Classes promoted to records
patterns.description: The reverse divergence: original final classes become records (joda `CurrencyUnit` and `Money`; loanamorti `Loan`, `EarlyPayment`, `LoanAmortization` and `MonthlyPayment`; fineract `LoanSchedulePlan*` periods and `PeriodDueDetails`). It is arguably more modern, but it adds record accessors to the API, some with cut component names (`totalDisbursedAmou()`, `totalOutstandingLoanBa()`: G01 and G02).
patterns.evidence: Records are a modernisation choice, not a gap.
patterns.hypothesis: Keep the rule, but complete the component names (G01) before promotion, and do not promote public library types whose original API used getters, when the estate is a library.

patterns.title: Visibility widened
patterns.description: Private static fields become public (`LOGGER`, `MC`, `MONTHS_PER_YEAR`, `PARSE_REGEX`, `COUNTRY_REGEX_LINE`), and package or private constructors and methods become public (`Money(BigMoney)`, `LoanScheduleModelDisbursementPeriod(...)`).
patterns.evidence: The cross-program references in the COBOL: ENTRY lists (FA-ENTRY) and the programs that touch a static item. A static used only inside its own program is private.
patterns.hypothesis: Give each member the least visibility that satisfies its cross-type references in the generated estate, and keep constants used by one type private.
patterns.outcome: R1 (least access from the estate reference graph) REJECTED 2026-11-01: it closed G21 but raised G22 on TRAIN and TEST. The authors' API intent is not in the COBOL; it needs an external API manifest.

patterns.title: Visibility narrowed
patterns.description: Public API methods that reached code calls only from inside their class become private: fineract `Money.isLessThanZero`, `MathUtil.isGreaterThanZero` and `ProgressiveLoanScheduleGenerator.generate`, and joda `BigMoney.getScale`. In a closed application this is harmless. In a library such as joda-money it breaks the API.
patterns.evidence: ENTRY tables list only the reached callers. The original intent is not in the COBOL.
patterns.hypothesis: Use an external policy input: library or application, or an API manifest. By default, do not narrow a public method of a public type below the visibility its name and the estate's convention suggest.
patterns.outcome: R1 (least access from the estate reference graph) REJECTED 2026-11-01: it closed G21 but raised G22 on TRAIN and TEST. The authors' API intent is not in the COBOL; it needs an external API manifest.

patterns.title: final lost on classes
patterns.description: Final original classes are emitted non-final: utility classes (`Annuity`, `Rounding`, `MathUtil`), value classes (`Schedule`, `LoanScheduleParams`) and nested builders.
patterns.evidence: Closed world: no other program extends or dispatches to a subclass of the type.
patterns.hypothesis: Make classes with no subclass in the estate final, and always make classes with only static members and a private constructor final. For library estates this over-approximates; it is acceptable.
patterns.outcome: R3 ACCEPTED 2026-11-01 behind the closedWorld estate profile: G23 TRAIN 20 -> 3, TEST 7 -> 0.

patterns.title: Fields made final
patterns.description: Original mutable fields become final (fineract-xl), either because their setters were never compiled (`FIELD.FINAL_ADDED_SETTER_UNREACHED`) or because reached code assigns them once.
patterns.evidence: This is a consequence of the J3S reach.
patterns.hypothesis: No rule: it is harmless, and arguably better.

patterns.title: Named constants inlined
patterns.description: Compile-time constants disappear and their literals appear in place: kontor-zins `MAX_MONTHS` (`months > 600`), `MONEY_SCALE` and `RATE_SCALE`.
patterns.evidence: javac folds compile-time constants before J3S reads the bytecode, so the COBOL holds only the literal.
patterns.hypothesis: Not closable. At most, name a literal repeated across a type as a private constant, but the original name cannot be recovered.

patterns.title: Exception messages dropped
patterns.description: `throw new IllegalArgumentException("principal must not be null")` becomes `throw new IllegalArgumentException()`: kontor-zins LoanTerms 7 to 0, Schedule 6 to 0, joda CurrencyUnit 10 to 3 and BigMoney 4 to 1, fineract ProgressiveEMICalculator 14 to 4.
patterns.evidence: None. J3S maps exceptions to class ids (`JO-SIMPLE-NAME`) and does not keep the message literal.
patterns.hypothesis: Not closable in the generator. It needs J3S to carry the message literal.

patterns.title: Not compiled by J3S (out of scope)
patterns.description: Methods, builders and nested types with no J3S frame, and methods whose frame J3S compiled as dead code (`* J3S: no object of ProcessedTransactionData is ever created`), which the generator emits as a `JX-DEAD` throw stub (`METHOD.DEAD_STUB`; their signatures count as preserved). This is the bulk of the "missing" API: joda-money has 107 public methods and 24 accessors, and fineract-xl has 344 public methods, 169 accessors and 114 Lombok members. It is not a generator gap: the estate's jobs never call them.
patterns.evidence: The FRAME comments are exhaustive for what J3S compiled.
patterns.hypothesis: Widen the J3S entry set (more job scenarios, or an API-driven entry list) when the full API matters. Nothing to do in the generator.

patterns.title: Extra constructors, fields and helpers
patterns.description: Members modern Java has and the original does not: explicit default constructors (private `<init>()` in enums and utility classes), a few extra public methods (`Money.currency()`), and record-promotion and Lombok-expansion leftovers. Private helpers split out differently are not observed: `METHOD.EXTRA_PRIVATE` is zero in all four estates.
patterns.evidence: These come from the generator's choices.
patterns.hypothesis: Low value. Omit an explicit no-argument constructor when it is the implicit one.

patterns.title: Reached members lost (not observed)
patterns.description: This is the check that the generator loses nothing J3S compiled: reached methods missing, overloads collapsed, fields, enum constants and builders lost, and reached types missing. Reached methods and overloads are zero in all four estates. The few `FIELD.MISSING` (fineract `ProcessedTransactionData.transactionType`, `transactionDate` and `reAgeParameter`) belong to a type J3S never instantiates (G27).
patterns.evidence: None needed.
patterns.hypothesis: Keep this at zero as a regression check.

patterns.title: Types moved to another package
patterns.description: A recovered type is placed in the package of its implementation or user: `ILoanConfigurationDetails` moves from `loanproduct.domain` to `loanproduct.data`, and `InterestScheduleModelRepositoryWrapper` from `loanaccount.service` to `loanschedule.domain`.
patterns.evidence: Frames print simple names only, so the package of a type J3S never compiled is unknown.
patterns.hypothesis: Not closable from the evidence, and of little importance.

patterns.title: final added where the original was extensible
patterns.description: A class made final although the original left it open to subclassing (TYPE.FINAL_ADDED). Introduced by R3.
patterns.evidence: None in the COBOL: external extension intent (framework proxies, library users) is not visible to the closed estate.
patterns.hypothesis: Acceptable modern practice only under the declared closedWorld estate profile (nothing outside subclasses or proxies). Without that profile R3 is off.

split: Rules are derived from COBOL evidence. The original Java only scores them, so the split decides which estates' scores may be read while a rule is designed.

- **Train (derive and tune): fineract-xl and kontor-zins.** fineract-xl holds most instances of G01–G03, G07, G09–G11, G16, G17, G21 and G22 (67 types, 673 truncated names, generics, Lombok, streams). kontor-zins is the only estate with original records (G19) and the record-style accessor case (G04).

- **Test (validate once a rule set is frozen; read their reports only then): joda-money and loanamorti.** joda-money is a library by another author with a different naming style. It tests G01/G02 transfer, G12 (short), G14 (Comparable, Serializable), G15 (BigMoneyProvider, exception superclasses), G20 and G22 (public API narrowing matters in a library). loanamorti tests G11 (factories returning the implementation), G15 (LoanAmortizationCalculator, RepeatableEarlyPayment), G16 (streams) and G20.
- **Patterns with fewer than five training instances** (G05, G08, G12, G14, G19): use leave-one-estate-out over the four estates instead, and report each fold.

- **Generalisation check for class (a) rules:** run them on an estate with no original Java (carddemo). There, the JOBOL audit index and the GN4 strangler SHADOW equivalence must not regress. A rule that needs the original to fire is class (b), not (a).

- **Success measure:** on the test estates, the pattern's count falls and reached API, signature and name fidelity rise, with JOBOL audit and SHADOW equivalence unchanged. Track `NAME.TRUNCATED.UNIQUE_WRONG` separately: a completion rule that raises it is wrong even if name fidelity rises.
method: - **Scope.** With `--cobol`, the original side is the classes in J3S CLASS headers plus the types the modern estate names (by fully qualified name, or by a unique simple name for moved types). Nested types follow their outer type. Methods are reached when a FRAME comment names the owner's simple name, the method name and the parameter types (by last dotted segment; a dangling `X>` matches a generic parameter whose last argument is X; varargs match arrays).

- **Alignment.** Types align by fully qualified name, then by unique simple name (moved), then nested by unique simple name (relocated). Methods align by name and erased parameter types, then by name and arity, then by the remaining overloads in order. Names only on the original side align with a damaged modern name (truncated, abbreviated or accessor-style) of the same arity. Fields, parameters, locals and constants align exactly first, then by damaged form (preferring the same type and the longest shared prefix, with no guess on a tie), then as the single remaining name of an erased type.

- **Name classes** (Names.java): exact; case (the same words); truncated (a strict prefix, at least two characters); abbreviated (each word a prefix or an ordered letter subset of the original word); accessor-style (x() against getX()); truncated+numbered (a cut stem plus a counter); numbered (a counter or temporary name); renamed. For truncated names, "completion" says whether the modern estate's other identifiers would complete the stem: unique-correct, unique-wrong, ambiguous-correct, ambiguous-wrong or none.

- **Lombok.** No delombok run was available. The original side synthesises the members Lombok would generate (getters, setters, constructors, builder(), equals, hashCode, canEqual and toString) with origin `lombok`. A modern nested `XBuilder` class of an original `@Builder` type is classed as Lombok expansion.

- **Distance** per matched type is a sum of penalties: kind changed 5; type visibility 2; type modifier 1; supertype lost 3, added 1; reached API method missing 3, other reached method missing 2; extra method 1 (0.5 if private); changed parameter or return types 2; member visibility or static 1; field missing 2, extra 0.5, type changed 1, flag 0.5; enum constant missing 2, extra 1; field or method name not exact 1; parameter or local name not exact 0.25; reached builder lost 3; and per idiom unit lost 0.5, capped at 10 per family. Unreached methods cost nothing. "Per member" divides by the original's member count.
- **Determinism.** There is no clock, inputs are visited in sorted order, and all output lists are sorted. Two runs give identical bytes (CompareTest.compareIsDeterministic).
